pattern: Myth vs fact supplement carousel, remade from the Turkish 'Hangi takviyeleri alırsam?' and 'Takviyeden önce...' doctor and dietitian listicles
why: The persona already searches 'which supplement should I take' on Instagram, so busting four common assumptions one per slide answers that question with their own data instead of another generic list.

slides.headline: Raf dolu takviye, hangisi sana uygun?
Efsane: Gen testi sadece köken merakı içindir
body: Gerçek: Beslenme, cilt ve sağlıklı yaşlanma raporları var.

slides.headline: Efsane: Rapor gelir, sen yalnız kalırsın
body: Gerçek: Doktor ve diyetisyenler sürecin içinde.
Sonuçlarını tek başına yorumlamak zorunda değilsin.

slides.headline: Efsane: Verilerin nereye gittiği belli değil
body: Gerçek: KVKK metni ve veri sayfası yayında.
Karar vermeden önce oku, sonra seç.

caption: Herkese iyi gelen tek bir takviye listesi yok. Dynova raporları kendi verinden hazırlanır, teşhis koymaz, karar vermene destek olur. Merak edersen dynova.health'e bir göz at.

findings.message: Promoting doctor and dietitian involvement may fall under Turkish health-provider advertising restrictions, so confirm this element is permitted and accurate before posting, or soften it to a neutral description of the consultation service.

findings.message: The pattern is remade from other creators' doctor and dietitian listicles; the slide copy reads as original, but make sure no wording, visuals or structure are copied directly from the source posts.

slides.issues: Type is big and clean on the dark gradient, and the purple accent works. The hook is a generic question that many supplement accounts already use, with no tension, number or myth tease to promise that swiping pays off. The open bottle and capsule shot is tidy but reads as a stock flat lay. The headline could tease the format, for example by naming the 4 myths.

slides.issues: This slide carries the real product: the Dynova site on a phone, clearly visible and on-brand. The headline over the blurred grey background is readable, though the body line is slightly small. The phone mockup is clean but feels a bit like a render, not handheld. Text on the phone screen is small but genuine. This is solid overall.

This is an obvious stock photo of a woman with glasses on a sofa with a laptop, and it has a recognizable stock-library look. The headline cuts across her body and laptop. The body copy sits over a busy area that includes a book with visible DOISNEAU lettering, which competes with the text. The image does not connect to genetic reports. Showing the Dynova report screen on a phone or laptop would make this slide far stronger.

final.notes: The gate passes: the real Dynova site appears on a phone on slide 2, and the dynova.health CTA is on slide 6. Typography is consistent and readable throughout. The main weaknesses are a soft hook on slide 1 and heavy reliance on stock photography on slides 3, 4 and 6, which drags native feel down. Replace those images with real product moments such as the kit, the report screen, a video consult or the KVKK page so each myth has visible proof. Strengthen slide 1 by teasing the myth-busting format, for example with 4 efsane. Trim the slide 4 body copy to avoid the orphaned final word.

The purple accent on 'takviye' is slightly low contrast against the mid-gray zone.

Slide 1 hook is generic; a stronger tension line or a relatable shelf visual would improve swipe rate. Fix the logo over the face on slide 6. Copy is sound and claims are appropriately hedged (rapor teşhis koymaz).
